selection.method: highest remaining verified actor-primary profiles after Batch 25

profiles.name: Art Carney
profiles.excerpt: Art Carney built a substantial radio career as an actor, mimic and comic singer before television made Ed Norton one of his defining roles.
profiles.bio_html:
Art Carney was born in Mount Vernon, New York in 1918 and entered professional entertainment as a comic singer with Horace Heidt's orchestra. Radio quickly revealed another strength: his gift for mimicry, including impressions of Franklin D. Roosevelt, Winston Churchill and other public figures.

Carney worked steadily in dramatic and comedy radio through the 1940s and early 1950s, appearing on Gang Busters, The Mysterious Traveler, Columbia Workshop and numerous other programs before The Honeymooners made him a television star. His early work as a professional singer remains a genuine second branch of his career.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves five Columbia Workshop performances credited to Carney, three each on Gang Busters and The Mysterious Traveler, two Words at War appearances and additional dramatic work.

profiles.name: Crauford Kent
profiles.excerpt: Crauford Kent brought decades of British and American stage and screen experience into Lux Radio Theatre and NBC University Theater.
profiles.bio_html:
Crauford Kent was born in London in 1881 and worked onstage in both Britain and the United States before becoming a prolific Hollywood character actor. Across the silent and sound eras he accumulated more than two hundred film appearances.

Radio used Kent's cultivated voice in prestige adaptation. He appeared repeatedly on Lux Radio Theatre and NBC University Theater, two series that depended on experienced stage and screen actors to give literary and film adaptations weight and clarity.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves eight Lux Radio Theatre performances credited to Kent and seven NBC University Theater appearances, documenting a substantial radio chapter late in his long acting career.

profiles.name: Ed Zimmerman
profiles.excerpt: Ed Zimmerman was a recurring Theater Five repertory actor during ABC’s weekday radio-drama revival of the mid-1960s.
profiles.bio_html:
Ed Zimmerman is best documented through Theater Five, ABC's ambitious weekday dramatic anthology of the 1960s. Personal biographical detail is limited, but the surviving cast record shows repeated professional work in the program's New York repertory.

Theater Five moved rapidly among crime, suspense, science fiction and contemporary drama. Recurring actors such as Zimmerman had to establish an entirely new character in each half-hour story, making versatility more important than star recognition.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 15 Theater Five performances credited to Zimmerman, providing a concentrated record of his contribution to later network radio drama.

profiles.name: Henry Leff
profiles.excerpt: Henry Leff combined radio acting with a four-decade career teaching broadcasting, while listeners knew him as police detective Ray Mallard on Candy Matson.
profiles.bio_html:
Henry Leff was born in Brooklyn and trained in theatre before settling in San Francisco, where he helped establish the broadcasting program at City College of San Francisco and led it for nearly four decades. His work as an educator shaped generations of Bay Area broadcasters.

Leff also maintained a professional acting career. His best-known continuing radio role was Lieutenant Ray Mallard, Candy Matson's police-detective love interest on Candy Matson, YUkon 2-8209. He also appeared in hard-boiled West Coast programs including Pat Novak, for Hire.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves six Candy Matson performances credited to Leff and two Pat Novak, for Hire appearances.

profiles.name: Hugh Thomas
profiles.excerpt: Hugh Thomas was a West Coast radio repertory actor whose surviving work spans literary anthology, suspense and major private-eye series.
profiles.bio_html:
Hugh Thomas belongs to the professional West Coast radio repertory whose broadcast record survives more clearly than later personal biography. His credits place him repeatedly in postwar dramatic production across several demanding formats.

Thomas appeared on NBC University Theater, Escape and The Adventures of Philip Marlowe, with additional work on Pat Novak, for Hire, This Is Your FBI and Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar. That spread required an actor comfortable with both literary adaptation and naturalistic crime drama.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves six NBC University Theater performances credited to Thomas, three each on Escape and The Adventures of Philip Marlowe, plus additional detective and FBI drama.

profiles.name: Jack Manning
profiles.excerpt: Jack Manning carried a classical stage career into radio and later became a stage director, producer and acting teacher as well as a character actor.
profiles.bio_html:
Jack Manning was born Jack Wilson Marks in Cincinnati in 1916 and began acting while studying at the University of Cincinnati. After moving to New York, he entered radio through programs including The Aldrich Family and became part of the city’s dramatic repertory.

Manning later built a broad theatre and television career and also worked professionally as a stage director, producer and acting teacher. His one-man Hamlet for early television became a particularly noted demonstration of his classical training.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves seven Theater Five performances credited to Manning, four Sears Radio Theater appearances, two CBS Radio Workshop broadcasts and additional work on Columbia Workshop and The Mysterious Traveler.

profiles.name: Jennifer Harmon
profiles.excerpt: Jennifer Harmon brought Broadway and daytime television experience into CBS Radio Mystery Theater as a recurring 1970s repertory actress.
profiles.bio_html:
Jennifer Harmon was born in Pasadena in 1943 and built a career across stage and television before and during her radio work. She became especially familiar to daytime audiences through roles on One Life to Live, Guiding Light and other serials.

During the 1970s Harmon became a recurring performer on CBS Radio Mystery Theater, where she moved among suspense, supernatural stories and contemporary drama rather than playing one continuing character.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 15 CBS Radio Mystery Theater performances credited to Harmon, documenting a substantial radio-drama chapter within her wider stage and screen career.

profiles.name: Lee Patrick
profiles.excerpt: Lee Patrick carried a long stage and film career into radio, moving from family serials to hard-boiled detective and suspense drama.
profiles.bio_html:
Lee Patrick was born in New York City in 1901 and built a long career on stage, film, radio and television. Film audiences especially remember her as Effie Perine in The Maltese Falcon, but radio gave her a substantial parallel body of work.

Patrick held a continuing role on the family serial The O’Neils and later appeared in detective and suspense programs including Let George Do It, The Line Up, Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar and Suspense.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves five Let George Do It performances credited to Patrick, three each on The Line Up and Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar, two Suspense appearances and additional anthology work.

profiles.name: Len Birman
profiles.excerpt: Len Birman built a transnational stage, screen and radio career and later became a familiar narrator and voice actor in Canadian and American broadcasting.
profiles.bio_html:
Len Birman began his acting career in Montreal and spent decades working across Canadian and American stage, film, television and radio. His classical theatre roles ranged from Shakespeare to Ibsen, while radio gave him a similarly broad dramatic repertory.

Birman worked extensively for CBC radio before appearing on American revival series including Sears Radio Theater and Mutual Radio Theater. He also narrated documentaries and educational programs and supplied commercial and animation voices, making narration a substantial second branch of his career.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 15 Sears Radio Theater performances credited to Birman, documenting the American radio-drama side of a much larger voice and acting career.

profiles.name: Marian Hailey
profiles.excerpt: Marian Hailey brought Broadway and film experience into CBS Radio Mystery Theater and later developed a substantial second career as an author.
profiles.bio_html:
Marian Hailey was born in Portland, Oregon in 1941 and trained in drama at the University of Washington before moving into professional theatre. Her Broadway and screen work included Company, Harvey and the film Lovers and Other Strangers.

Hailey became a recurring performer on CBS Radio Mystery Theater during the 1970s and early 1980s. Later, as Marian Hailey-Moss, she authored numerous children’s books and other works, making writing a genuine second creative profession.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 15 CBS Radio Mystery Theater performances credited under the source form Marianne Haley. Her public profile uses the canonical professional name Marian Hailey.
